name: Scope and PR mode execution matrix
description: Introduces two orthogonal flags — scope and mode — giving FADE a 3x2 execution matrix. Scope controls how much work FADE processes before stopping (story, prd, all). Mode controls how changes land (auto = direct to main, pr = branch + pull request). Together they make FADE usable in enterprise workflows with branch protection, while preserving the existing autonomous loop for personal use.

context.opportunity: FADE currently has one execution mode: process stories and commit directly to main. This works well for personal projects but is incompatible with enterprise workflows that require branch protection and PR review. Adding scope + mode flags unlocks FADE for use at Milliman and similar orgs without sacrificing autonomy for personal use.

problem: FADE commits directly to main, bypassing branch protection in enterprise repos
No way to run FADE for a single story or single PRD without it processing everything
Autonomous loop is all-or-nothing — no gate for human review before code lands on main
solution: Add --scope flag (story | prd | all) to control stopping point
Add --mode flag (auto | pr) to control whether FADE commits to main or creates a branch and raises a PR
In PR mode: create branch at start, commit per story as now, raise PR at the scope boundary using gh CLI
Auto-generate PR description from PRD name and completed story list
Add convenience shortcuts: fade pr (prd + pr), fade story --pr (story + pr)
Existing fade yolo remains unchanged (all + auto)

userStories.title: Scope flag controls stopping point
userStories.story: As a developer, I want to pass --scope=story|prd|all so that FADE stops and signals completion at the right boundary
acceptanceCriteria: --scope=story stops after STORY_DONE and exits cleanly
--scope=prd stops after ALL_COMPLETE for the current PRD and exits cleanly
--scope=all processes all PRDs in the queue (existing behaviour)
Default scope is all to preserve existing behaviour
Invalid scope value prints usage and exits non-zero

userStories.title: Mode flag controls how changes land
userStories.story: As a developer, I want to pass --mode=auto|pr so that FADE either commits directly to main or works on a branch
acceptanceCriteria: --mode=auto commits directly to main (existing behaviour)
--mode=pr creates a branch before starting work
Branch name format: fade/prd-{prd-id}-{slug} for prd scope, fade/story-{us-id} for story scope
Default mode is auto to preserve existing behaviour
In PR mode, all story commits land on the branch, not main

userStories.title: PR raised at scope boundary in PR mode
userStories.story: As a developer, I want FADE to raise a pull request when it reaches the scope boundary so that my changes go through review before merging
acceptanceCriteria: At scope boundary in PR mode, FADE runs gh pr create
PR title is auto-generated: PRD name (prd scope) or story title (story scope)
PR body lists completed stories with their acceptance criteria
FADE confirms PR URL to stdout before exiting
If gh CLI is not installed, FADE exits with a clear error message before starting work
If gh pr create fails, FADE reports the error and does not silently continue

userStories.title: Convenience shortcuts for common modes
userStories.story: As a developer, I want short commands for the most common mode combinations so that I don't have to type flags every time
acceptanceCriteria: fade pr is equivalent to fade --scope=prd --mode=pr
fade story --pr is equivalent to fade --scope=story --mode=pr
fade yolo remains unchanged (--scope=all --mode=auto)
fade run with no flags defaults to --scope=all --mode=auto (existing behaviour)
All shortcuts are documented in README and fade --help output

technicalNotes.rationale: Medium complexity bash changes — sonnet is appropriate
constraints: PR mode requires gh CLI to be installed and authenticated — check at startup, fail fast
Do not modify existing fade yolo or fade run behaviour — additive only
Branch creation must happen before any file changes so nothing is committed to main in PR mode
This PRD must be implemented manually, not via FADE itself — FADE cannot fix its own execution loop

risks.risk: gh CLI not available in all environments
risks.mitigation: Fail fast at startup with clear install instructions if gh is missing and --mode=pr is requested

risks.risk: Branch already exists from a previous interrupted run
risks.mitigation: Check for existing branch before creating, append timestamp suffix if collision

definitionOfDone: fade pr and fade story --pr work end-to-end against a test repo with branch protection
fade yolo and fade run with no flags behave identically to pre-change
README updated with matrix table and new flag documentation
